abstract:
Oral dysbiosis has been associated with inflammatory processes in acute exacerbations of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (AECOPD). However, whether Aspergillus-associated or Candida-positive status is associated with distinct oral multi-omics profiles, and whether these profiles change following treatment, remains unclear.
In this prospective cohort study (August 2024 to July 2025), 18 AECOPD patients were enrolled and stratified into non-fungal exacerbators (n=6), Aspergillus-associated AECOPD (n=6), and Candida-positive AECOPD (n=6). Oral samples were collected before treatment and, where available, after treatment. The primary analyses compared pretreatment microbial and metabolic profiles across fungal-status groups, whereas longitudinal pre/post-treatment analyses were secondary and exploratory and were performed only in groups with sufficient paired samples.
Baseline characteristics were comparable across groups. At pretreatment, Aspergillus-associated AECOPD showed significantly reduced α diversity and distinct microbial community separation from non-fungal exacerbators (Bray-Curtis R = 0.378, P = 0.009), whereas Candida-positive AECOPD showed no significant global shift. At the genus level, exploratory LEfSe analysis identified distinct subgroup-associated candidate taxonomic signatures. PICRUSt2-based predicted functional profiles were broadly similar across groups. Metabolomic profiling showed the most pronounced baseline differences in the Aspergillus-associated group, with 11 upregulated and 90 downregulated metabolites versus the non-fungal group. Differential metabolites in this baseline comparison were predominantly mapped to sphingolipid metabolism, purine metabolism, one-carbon metabolism, and cAMP/cGMP signaling pathways. In secondary exploratory longitudinal analyses, metabolic shifts were observed in the non-fungal group (4 upregulated and 78 downregulated metabolites) and the Candida-positive group (14 upregulated and 8 downregulated metabolites). No formal longitudinal analysis was performed in the Aspergillus-associated group because only two post-treatment samples were available. O2PLS identified shared cross-omics variation distinguishing pretreatment Aspergillus-associated from non-fungal AECOPD, with several microbial and metabolite features contributing to the shared latent component.
Compared with non-fungal and Candida-positive AECOPD, Aspergillus-associated AECOPD showed the most pronounced pretreatment oral microbial dysbiosis and metabolic alterations. These findings support the presence of a distinct oral microbial-metabolic phenotype associated with Aspergillus status and provide candidate signatures for future validation in larger longitudinal cohorts.
